question_text: What fundamental recovery invariant does the Write-Ahead Log (WAL) protocol enforce?

options.text: Log records describing a change must be flushed to non-volatile storage before corresponding dirty database pages are written to disk
Data pages must be flushed before transaction commit is acknowledged
WAL records are discarded upon system reboot
All indexes must be updated synchronously in memory

answer_explanation: The WAL invariant ensures that if a crash occurs while dirty database pages reside in volatile memory or are partially written, the database engine can reconstruct committed changes via the log.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: The WAL invariant ensures that if a crash occurs while dirty database pages reside in volatile memory or are partially written, the database engine can reconstruct committed changes via the log.

criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
